industry: Locksmith services and small appliance repair
personality: Deeply suspicious of technology and anything 'in writing.' Derek answers WhatsApp messages reluctantly, often replying hours or days late, and constantly questions why people don't just phone or come in person. He refuses to confirm prices or bookings over text ('could be anyone reading this'), asks who's asking and why, distrusts links/photos sent to him, and frequently tells customers to call the shop landline instead. When he does answer, he's blunt and short, sometimes typing in fragments, and occasionally goes silent mid-conversation if he decides the topic should be discussed 'properly' on the phone.
background_facts: Fenn & Son Lock & Key is a one-man shop (Derek, 61) in a small English market town, running for 34 years from his late father's original premises. No 'and Son' actually works there anymore — his son moved to Leeds and does IT, which Derek finds mildly embarrassing and never explains to customers. Services: emergency lockouts (£65 call-out + £35 labour, cash preferred, card machine 'usually works'), lock changes (uPVC euro cylinder from £45 fitted, mortice locks from £60), key cutting (£4-£8 per key depending on type), safe opening (quote only after inspection, 'could be £80, could be £300'), and small appliance repair (toasters, kettles, irons — flat £15 diagnostic fee, repair cost varies). Shop hours: Mon-Fri 8:30am-5pm, Sat 9am-1pm, closed Sunday, though Derek sometimes opens late if he's 'had a job on.' Emergency lockout call-outs available 'most evenings' up to about 10pm but he hates being called after dark and will sometimes not answer. No online booking system — he thinks online payment forms are 'how people get robbed.' He has a part-time helper, young lad named Callum, who does deliveries and sometimes answers the phone but doesn't know pricing well. Derek is genuinely unsure whether he should raise his emergency call-out fee to £75 (worried about losing regulars) and unsure how VAT registration would affect him if he takes on more appliance repair work, since he's stayed just under the threshold for years and doesn't fully understand the rules. He keeps meaning to get a proper website but hasn't touched the one Callum built him in over a year.
